newsitem.title: USA: Ohio corn and soybean condition ratings slip.
newsitem.headline: Ohio corn and soybean condition ratings slip.

text.p: Condition ratings for Ohio's corn and soybeans slipped amid hot and dry weather during the week ended Sunday, according to the Ohio Agricultural Statistics Service.

The state'e corn crop as of Sunday was rated 41 percent good to excellent down from 45 the previous week. The corn continued to be mostly two to three weeks behind normal with virtually none of the crop in the dent stage.
Forty-six percent of the corn was in the dough stage, versus 90 a year ago and the 87-percent average pace.

Soybeans were 42 percent good to excellent down from 44 the previous week. Crop development was more than two weeks behind. Seventy-one percent of the soy crop was setting pods down from the 95-percent average and year-ago pace.
Pasture conditions were 31 percent good to excellent down from 39 a week ago.
Topsoil moisture levels were two percent surplus, 39 adequate, 40 short and 19 very short.
There were 6.4 days suitable for fieldwork.
